claims.text: The as-deposited Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer coatings are approximately 1 μm thick and contain FCC and BCC phases.
An 8 nm modulation period produces coherent interfaces with continuous atomic planes.
A 16 nm modulation period produces semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces containing misfit dislocations.
The 32 and 80 nm multilayers are dominated by grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary domination at 32 and 80 nm occurs because those modulation periods exceed a typical grain diameter of approximately 20 nm.
Semicoherent interfaces cause dislocation pileup during deformation.
Dislocation pileup at semicoherent interfaces generates localized high stress.
Localized high stress triggers stress-induced amorphization at the interfaces.
Interfacial amorphization redistributes local stress.
The amorphous interfacial regions possess free volume and lower atomic-migration barriers.
Amorphous interfacial regions facilitate creep through atomic diffusion or interface slip.
Interfacial amorphization shifts the dominant creep mechanism from dislocation-mediated slip to atomic diffusion or interface slip.
Coherent interfaces in the 8 nm multilayer permit relatively smooth dislocation transmission.
Grain-boundary-dominated structures in the 32 and 80 nm multilayers promote dislocation slip or climb.
The 16 nm semicoherent multilayer will have greater room-temperature creep resistance than the 8, 32, and 80 nm multilayers.
The creep stress exponent of the 16 nm multilayer will approach 1–2.
A creep stress exponent near 1–2 is consistent with diffusion- or interface-slip-mediated creep.
The 8, 32, and 80 nm multilayers will exhibit higher creep stress exponents indicative of dislocation-mediated creep.
The proposed behavior is limited to sputtered approximately 1 μm-thick Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayers under the specified room-temperature nanoindentation conditions.
Previous molecular-dynamics and HRTEM studies suggest that stress-induced interfacial amorphization occurs.

contradictions.description: The amorphous interfaces are said to lower migration barriers and facilitate diffusion/interface-slip creep, yet they are also claimed to increase creep resistance. The hypothesis does not explain why facilitating these deformation pathways produces less time-dependent deformation overall.
